scope: Benchmark fixtures, orchestration and report tooling only; findings here are not production execution defects.

findings: Stack cache recursively builds Python tuples along every prefix; unusually deep stacks can hit recursion limit, and missing/empty samples or zero measured CPU fail via trace[-1], division or max. Acceptance: iterative stack traversal and explicit no-valid-samples report.

CPU samples are included by endpoint timestamp rather than requiring full CPU-delta interval inside measured phase; boundary samples can include warmup CPU. Acceptance: clip intervals or require previous/current timestamps inside phase and report excluded duration.
Workload scales and 500 Hz/10 Hz labels hardcoded rather than derived from capture metadata.

Incomplete curated engine pairs are silently skipped even while header counts all configurations and upstream missing statuses are explicitly visible. Duplicate (config,case,engine) rows overwrite silently. Acceptance: validate unique complete pairs or render missing/duplicate statuses and exclude them transparently from totals.
Uses imported CONFIGS and fixed host/runtime/heap/warmup narratives instead of provenance/worker metadata; renderer can mislabel captures after runtime/config changes.
Missing perf event values use total(event) default zero; absent cache-misses and genuine zero are conflated. Acceptance: preserve unavailable counter status and multiplex/scaling validity.
Host model, cores, heap, toolchain, warmup duration narratives hardcoded; script accepts arbitrary compatible result directories without validating these claims.
Assumes nonempty metrics/events and hardcodes 10 Hz label; missing capture data crashes without explicit incomplete status.

Uses fixed CONFIGS and source-partition label; does not verify worker parameters agree. Instructions/query estimated with median latency times mean rate, unlike measured-throughput estimate elsewhere; label remains estimated but cross-report comparisons need same definition.
Hardcodes 20 samples, 100k/50k rows, local14 and heap48GiB in generated report regardless of worker metadata. Acceptance: derive configuration/provenance or enforce expected capture fingerprint.

Resume verifies claimed commit, seconds and configs but retains old captures after script hashes change; records script_hashes_on_resume without invalidating prior results. --commit is caller-supplied and not checked against actual installed native wheel/source. Acceptance: each capture retains immutable source/binary/runner hashes and mixed-provenance resumes reject or explicitly separate series.
Capture/provenance subprocesses have no timeout; a hung collector blocks the suite indefinitely. Acceptance: bounded process-tree lifecycle and explicit failed capture record.

Allows existing output directory and overwrites provenance with fresh runs list; partial prior artifacts can become mixed with new run. Acceptance: fresh-run directory or configuration/hash-validated resume, atomic report replacement.
Compilers checked before captures and reported afterward, but runtime contention is not rejected during capture. Process-name heuristic is only a partial idle-host guarantee.

Resume retains previous case results while replacing runner/upstream hash fields with current hashes, checking only engine/smoke/data directory. Native fixture cache completeness is marker-only, without fixture builder/source/binary identity. Acceptance: pin capture and fixture fingerprints and reject/migrate stale cache explicitly.

Worker cleanup kills process group only while primary worker is alive (normal completed path simply joins); primary can exit while JVM/helpers remain. SIGTERM cleanup escalates only if primary remains alive, so surviving descendants can contaminate later cases. Acceptance: verify/reap owned process group after primary termination too.

AST adapter removes pytest decorators and manually reconstructs fixture/parameter behavior; upstream source changes can silently diverge (for example parametrization argnames list unsupported by inventory branch using split). Acceptance: fail closed on unsupported decorators/signatures and cross-check collected case IDs/arguments with pytest collection.
Published fixture downloads lack expected content checksum/version, so exact dimensions alone do not establish stable exact fixture content. Acceptance: record/verify input digests.

Failed cases are recorded but script exits successfully; calling harness cannot equate subprocess zero status with all cases passed. Acceptance: aggregate exit status reflects failures while preserving report.

Several named workloads only assert force-count output, not projected field/scan/lookup values. Whether operators are actually forced depends on _force_count implementation/optimizer; ensure value-consuming checksum or verified physical plan for performance claims. This is benchmark validation gap, not a demonstrated production defect.
Input validation omits positive iterations/scale/cores and legal VCF position range; zero iterations produces caught failure instead of early configuration error.

limitations: Read-only audit; no benchmark captures launched, no production edits, no report claims established by executing these historical workloads.
Collector profile_* modules belong to root audit; interpretation of underlying raw counters requires those modules.
